messages.content: 你能計算人類與黑猩猩之間的基因相似性，以及人類與大猩猩之間的基因相似性嗎？請以DNA序列為依據，提供結果的百分比和分數格式。

function.name: genetics_calculate_similarity
function.description: Calculates the genetic similarity between two species based on their DNA sequences. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

format.description: The format of the result (percentage or fraction). Default is percentage.

message.reasoning:
The user wants calculation of genetic similarity between humans and chimpanzees, and humans and gorillas, using DNA sequence as basis, providing results in percentage and fraction formats.

We have a tool "genetics_calculate_similarity" which calculates genetic similarity between two species based on their DNA sequences. It takes species1, species2, optional format ("percentage" default). We need to call this function twice: once with species1="human", species2="chimpanzee", format="percentage"; second with species1="human", species2="gorilla", format="fraction".

But we don't know if the function expects actual DNA sequences or just species names? The description says "based on their DNA sequences". But the arguments only include species names; maybe the function internally knows the sequences. So we can pass species names.

Thus we should call the function twice. We'll use the function calls accordingly.

We'll produce two calls:

First: genetics_calculate_similarity({"species1":"human","species2":"chimpanzee","format":"percentage"})
Second: genetics_calculate_similarity({"species1":"human","species2":"gorilla","format":"fraction"})

We then output the results. We'll do separate calls.
